title: 2026 Georgia gubernatorial election
description: Georgia voters will elect a governor on November 3, 2026, in an open-seat race because Republican incumbent Brian Kemp is term-limited. The general election pits Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, against Republican Rick Jackson, a billionaire healthcare CEO who defeated Trump-endorsed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in a June 16 primary runoff after spending more than $100 million of his own money. The contest is a major test of partisan control in a closely divided swing state that has not elected a Democratic governor since 1998, though Democrats showed new strength by winning two statewide Public Service Commission seats in 2025 (Georgia Recorder) and, for the first time since 2006, exceeding Republican turnout in the 2026 primary by drawing more than 1 million ballots to the GOP's nearly 940,000 (Georgia Recorder). Key contrasts include Bottoms' support for Medicaid expansion and public education investment versus Jackson's emphasis on tax cuts, public safety, and his self-funded outsider status.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race as of 2026-06-19.

candidates.name: Keisha Lance Bottoms
candidates.summary: Keisha Lance Bottoms is a Democratic candidate for governor of Georgia and the former mayor of Atlanta. Her campaign says she is focused on affordability, health care, education, public safety, housing, environmental stewardship, and veterans' issues.

Healthcare.stance: Keisha Lance Bottoms says she would lower health care costs by expanding Medicaid, ending Georgia Pathways, and replacing it with broader coverage. Her plan also includes stabilizing rural hospitals, expanding telehealth and EMS access, reducing prescription drug costs, and strengthening mental health and maternal health services.

sources.title: Issues - Keisha for Governor

Economy.stance: Her economic agenda emphasizes small business support, workforce development, and housing affordability. She has proposed restructuring the Department of Economic Development, creating an Office of Small Business, expanding loan and grant programs, and establishing an affordable housing trust fund.

sources.title: Issues - Keisha for Governor

Climate/Energy.stance: Keisha Lance Bottoms says she would treat climate and environmental policy as a governing priority by investing in flood mitigation, brownfield redevelopment, and water infrastructure. She also says Georgia should slow the rapid expansion of data centers to limit pressure on utility bills, water resources, and surrounding communities.

sources.title: Issues - Keisha for Governor

Immigration.stance: No public position found on a Georgia governor immigration platform beyond her past actions as Atlanta mayor limiting the city’s cooperation with ICE detainee housing. Her campaign issues page does not appear to include a dedicated immigration plank.

Election Policy.stance: She supports expanding early voting and absentee voting, making Election Day a state holiday, and protecting local election officials from political interference. She backs a Georgia Housing Fast Track, expanded renter and down payment assistance, more support for local law enforcement, and stronger flood mitigation and water infrastructure.

Education.stance: She says she would fully fund Georgia schools, modernize the state’s education funding formula, expand literacy and financial literacy, support universal childcare, eliminate the state income tax for teachers, and create a path to free technical and community college.

candidates.name: Rick Jackson
candidates.summary: Rick Jackson is a billionaire healthcare executive and founder of Jackson Healthcare who is the Republican nominee for governor of Georgia in 2026. He grew up in foster care in Atlanta and later built a healthcare staffing company generating over $3 billion in annual revenue. Jackson defeated Trump-endorsed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in a primary runoff after spending more than $100 million of his own money, and will face Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms in the general election.

Economy.stance: The plan prioritizes affordability and economic growth by freezing property taxes immediately to halt rising assessments and cutting the state income tax by 50% within four years, with the goal of eliminating it within eight years. It also calls for using technology and AI to reduce waste in government and freezing tuition, room, and board at public colleges to curb rising education costs.

flags.concern: The stance describes Jackson as having 'publicly echoed claims that Georgia's 2020 election was stolen, which election officials and courts have rejected.' While the sources cited (Democracy Docket, NBC News) are credible, the phrasing 'which election officials and courts have rejected' is a factual assertion about the outcome of those proceedings. The sources should be verified to confirm they explicitly state this rejection, rather than relying on the profile's editorial framing. This is a high-stakes claim and warrants explicit source confirmation.
flags.suggestion: Verify that the cited sources (Democracy Docket and NBC News articles) explicitly document the rejection by election officials and courts, or reframe as: 'Jackson has publicly echoed claims about Georgia's 2020 election; election officials and courts have rejected these claims (per [source]).'

flags.concern: The stance uses the phrase 'fight to restore a woman's right to choose' — this is candidate framing language from Bottoms' campaign. For consistency and neutrality, compare against Jackson's stance which uses 'pro-life' and 'Heartbeat-law framework' (his framing). Both are appropriately attributed to the candidates' own language, but the profile should ensure this asymmetry is intentional and consistent across all issues.
flags.suggestion: Confirm this reflects the candidates' own campaign language (which it appears to do based on the source URLs to their official sites). If so, this is acceptable as it represents each candidate's self-description. No change needed if this is intentional.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the 2026 Georgia gubernatorial race. Both candidates' positions are documented with citations to official campaign websites, credible news outlets, and public records. The profile demonstrates strong internal consistency: Bottoms' stances on abortion, healthcare, education, and climate are all sourced to her official campaign site; Jackson's positions on tax policy, DEI, and healthcare are sourced to his campaign site and reputable news outlets (Forbes, NBC News, Democracy Docket). Background information is accurate and properly attributed. Language is generally neutral across both candidates, with appropriate use of candidate framing (e.g., 'pro-life' for Jackson, 'pro-choice' language for Bottoms) without asymmetric loading. The profile appropriately documents gaps (e.g., 'no public position found' on foreign policy for Bottoms, limited climate detail for Jackson) rather than fabricating positions. Donor summaries are well-documented with specific figures and source attribution.

flags.concern: The stance mentions 'extreme abortion ban' in a source title (georgiademocrat.org). While the profile itself uses neutral language, the source title contains loaded terminology.
flags.suggestion: No action required as the profile's own summary remains neutral, but be mindful of source titles when selecting citations.

flags.concern: The stance uses the term 'election denier'. While this is a common journalistic descriptor, it can be perceived as non-neutral.
flags.suggestion: Consider rephrasing to 'has echoed claims that the 2020 election was stolen' to maintain a strictly descriptive tone, though the current phrasing is supported by the cited source.

flags.concern: The stance uses the term 'illegal immigrant'.
flags.suggestion: Ensure consistency in terminology across the profile; consider using 'unauthorized immigrants' or 'undocumented immigrants' to align with neutral standards, though the current usage is common in political reporting.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available, so this forecast relies on non-polling indicators and carries substantial uncertainty. Georgia remains a closely divided swing state, but Republicans retain a modest baseline edge in a gubernatorial race and the state has not elected a Democratic governor since 1998. This is also an open-seat contest, which reduces incumbency advantages and keeps the race competitive. Democrats have meaningful positive signals in the provided race data, including winning two statewide Public Service Commission seats in 2025 and surpassing Republican turnout in the 2026 primary, suggesting real competitiveness. At the same time, Jackson's massive self-funding, high visibility after a hard-fought primary, and the GOP's longer-term statewide gubernatorial strength support a slight Republican edge. With no public polling and both nominees lacking prior statewide elected-office experience, the most defensible informational rating is a narrow Republican advantage with low confidence.
